This modest length at parturition reflects the substantial yolk reserves that sustain the developing embryo throughout its prolonged incubation. Maintained at a stable environmental temperature of 12 °C [T = 12 °C], the onset of independent foraging occurs at approximately 168 days [ab = approximately 168 days], a duration that reflects the relatively low metabolic rates of this cold-water species and allows for thorough organogenesis before the yolk reserves are exhausted.

As juvenile Leucoraja erinacea grow, they experience a steady increase in body size before reaching the dimensions linked to reproductive maturation. Field surveys indicate that the total length at which females attain sexual maturation is approximately 40.7 cm [Lp = approximately 40.7 cm], a measurement derived from examination of gonadal development in captured individuals. This length corresponds closely with the point at which the onset of ovarian maturation and testicular recrudescence become histologically evident. The age at which this first reproduction event occurs has been calculated at 2,920 days after hatching [tR = 2,920 days after hatching] when individuals are reared at a stable environmental temperature of 12 °C [T = 12 °C], reflecting a life-history strategy characterized by delayed maturity relative to many other elasmobranchs of comparable body plan.

This relatively extended lifespan is consistent with the species' slow pace of life and low natural mortality rates observed in wild populations. At the upper end of the size spectrum, the ultimate total length attained by this skate reaches 54 centimeters [Li = 54 centimeters], with the corresponding maximum wet weight of a fully grown adult recorded at 910 grams [Wwi = 910 grams]. These maximum body dimensions place Leucoraja erinacea among the smaller rajinids, a trait that may influence its ecological role as both predator of benthic invertebrates and prey for larger demersal fishes.

Body condition varies predictably with size during ontogeny, and length-weight relationships provide useful indices of health for population monitoring. For an individual measuring 42 centimeters in total length, the predicted wet weight is approximately 400 grams , a figure that aligns well with empirical measurements from specimens ranging between 40.6 and 43.2 centimeters that typically weigh between 0.34 and 0.45 kilograms. This relationship between length and mass underscores the relatively robust build of this species compared to more gracile skates. The reproductive output of Leucoraja erinacea is modest, reflecting its slow life-history trajectory. At the experimental temperature of 12 °C [T = 12 °C], females produce approximately 30 offspring per year [Ri = approximately 30 offspring per year], representing a sustained but low-intensity annual fecundity typical of many oviparous elasmobranchs.

Similarly, the attainment of sexual maturation at a total length of approximately 40.7 centimeters [Lp = approximately 40.7 centimeters] and the onset of first reproduction at 2,920 days after hatching [tR = 2,920 days after hatching] position this species as a late-maturing elasmobranch with a generation time exceeding several years at a temperature of 12 °C [T = 12 °C].
